deities: Goddess Laikhurembi - Meitei goddess with the special power of Yungyatnaba (erect and sharp): she could see objects accurately no matter how far away they were, perceive who a person truly was inside, and announce wise judgments so people received their right rewards (per simple.wikipedia.org)
festivals: Lai Haraoba of Uripok - the temple's annual festival; a carnival-like atmosphere accompanies the traditional sacred rituals, with maibis dancing to the gentle music of the pena, becoming possessed by spirits and delivering oracles (per Wikipedia)

history.dynasty: Ancient Meitei; associated legend: King Thongalel sent his second wife Leinaotabi to accompany her brother-in-law Poireiton as a wife instead of Laikhurembi (per Leimarel Mingkhei and Folk Culture of Manipur, 1993)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Laikhurembi is a goddess of the Meitei (Sanamahi) religion, not a Hindu deity, and her shrine at Uripok is a Sanamahi site, not a Hindu temple. CSV correction: the actual town is Uripok in Imphal West district, Manipur (Uripok Kangchup Street, Tourangbam Leikai, Imphal 795004; geocoded 24.80776, 93.92997) - NOT Thoubal as the CSV states. Per Wikipedia's article on the goddess, a temple dedicated to Goddess Laikhurembi stands in Uripok town in Imphal West district; no source places a Laikhurembi temple in Thoubal. The goddess had special powers: Yungyatnaba (erect and sharp), meaning she could see objects accurately regardless of distance and see who a person truly was inside, announcing wise judgments. During Uripok's Lai Haraoba festival, maibis dance in the melodies of the pena, become possessed when the music stops, and act as oracles. No reliable image of this specific temple was found, so media is left empty. Identity certainty: medium-high - Wikipedia and the geocoder agree on Uripok, Imphal West, but no descriptive travel source for the shrine itself was found.
